data.narrative:
Oklo is a public-stage nuclear energy company currently valued at $7.0B following its SPAC merger. The target operates within a narrow sector comprising 9 identified comparable companies—3 public peers (including NNE and SMR) and 6 private competitors such as Valar Atomics, X-Energy, and NuScale Power—though the private universe remains fragmented across multiple technology approaches and development stages.

Peer-median valuation analysis is not applicable here. The nuclear energy subsector lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables meeting standard triangulation thresholds; only 2 similar-tier companies exist within the filtered peer set, falling short of the minimum 3 datapoints required for statistical reliability. Applying an all-sector median would introduce material bias given the heterogeneous nature of nuclear technology platforms and regulatory pathways. The composition of Oklo's comp universe—concentrated in early-stage private development and a thin public float—limits the applicability of traditional multiples-based approaches.

The $7.0B current valuation sits within a market context of significant uncertainty. Without sufficient peer-median support, valuation relies on qualitative assessment of technology differentiation, regulatory pathway clarity, and capital efficiency relative to the broader cohort. Key uncertainties include regulatory approval timelines, the path to revenue generation across the 9-company competitive set, and whether Oklo's approach commands a sustainable valuation premium. A narrower, deeper analysis of private-round pricing and public-market comps individually would be required to triangulate a defensible range.
